text: In Genesis 22 a question is raised for which no answer is supplied. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; yet no account is given of what passes within him, and the narrator gives no description of his inward life. He neither protests nor bargains. Of the Abraham who pleaded for Sodom nothing appears. He is presented less as a character than as a silence, and that silence is the chapter’s centre.
